items.title: What Makes a Good Resume? Asking for a friend!
items.pt:
There are a lot of resume advice out there. A lot of different opinions of how Resume should be structure whether you are still a student, early career, or just deep into your career in tech.

To make things simpler, I want to ask the community on Resume advice and how to make your resume stand out in the age of AI. There are a lot of advice on making your resume "good", so this would be an open question to all. Looking forward to hear your advice on making a great Resume!!!

items.title: The onboarding step I stopped skipping: writing down the handoff
items.pt:
A small freelance project can feel straightforward right up until the first handoff.

The brief looked clear. The client seemed aligned. The deadline was reasonable. Then a familiar set of questions appeared in different places:


Which file is the current one?
Who is approving this?
What exactly counts as “done”?
Where should the final copy live?
What happens if the scope changes halfway through?


None of these questions is difficult on its own. The expensive part is answering them repeatedly,

items.title: Designer-RSI: Evolving Procedural Memory from User Traffic for Agentic Graphic Design
items.pt: Professional graphic design is a long-horizon agentic task in which structured, editable artifacts emerge from many interdependent actions, yet outcomes admit no reliable programmatic oracle. items.pt: We present MintAct, a family of vision-language models that unifies UI grounding, multi-step navigation across mobile, desktop, and web, and visual tool use, trained at 2B, 4B, and 8B scales. Through careful design of our environments, data, and training recipes, MintAct models match the performance of per-domain specialists across all of these capabilities. items.title: CodeMidas: Scaling Agentic Coding RL Environments from Code Itself
items.pt: Training capable coding agents via reinforcement learning (RL) requires diverse tasks with reliable verifiers. Open-source codebases offer a rich source of such tasks, while existing methods typically rely on development artifacts such as issues and commits, limiting the range of tasks that can be extracted.
